content.thinking:
I'm setting up the file imports, bringing in Three.js utilities, the builder module, and skeleton types needed to construct the geometry with glow strength merged into the bag data.

Writing geometry bag and transform helpers...

Still defining helper functions...

Now I'm setting up the skeleton builder, creating the root joint and starting on the skull joint with its position and orientation.

Working through skull and jaw joint placements, then defining the cranium part as a scaled sphere positioned at the skull coordinates, and starting to think through the snout loft stations.

I'm lofting the snout with three stations tapering forward, placing the nose tip and nostrils as small dark spheres near the front, and starting to position brow spikes.

Now I'm working out the eye sockets as dark ellipsoids with glowing teal eye balls slightly slanted via rotation, plus a brow ridge bar positioned above each eye.

Then I'm placing the upper teeth along the snout using interpolated positions, computing tooth base points along the snout's curved lower surface with varying lengths and a slight downward-forward direction.

For the lower jaw, I'm setting joint and loft stations so the mouth opens slightly downward, with upward-pointing teeth and a small gap between jaw and snout that widens toward the tip, plus placing a soul flame orb glowing inside the mouth cavity.

I'm placing cheek spike flares, horns with ivory banding, back crest cones trailing down the skull, a glowing forehead gem, and considering a gold brow-band torus wrapping around the cranium.

Writing glyph path strings...

Now I'm figuring out the dais rune disc and post placement geometry—sizing ghost cards, and positioning flame posts at the hexagon corners between tier1 and tier2 radii so they sit just outside the tier2 edge.

Each post gets a bone-spike cone base with a gold cap ring and a glowing flame card frame at the tip, giving six posts six flames using the glow() helper on card meshes. I'm also scattering floating octahedra shards near the shaft and blade, plus adding bone fragment rubble and possibly a small dragon-hatchling skull near a dais corner for extra detail.

I'm writing the obsidian paint function that uses cellular noise to create cracks, filling them with a teal color and blending two obsidian base tones elsewhere.

Now I'm defining the bone paint for the skull with a mottled ivory texture, then moving to the grip wrap pattern—computing a helical phase along the handle length to alternate seam and crimson stripe colors with blending between them.

I'm thinking through adding a thin gold thread stitch line between the two crimson tones, plus a rune band near the grip ends, and setting blade thickness. I'm also planning two hanging crimson ribbons with gold edges and swallow-tail cuts attached at the gold clasp near the grip top, with slight thickness and positioning for a draped, slightly wavy look.

Positioning ribbon extrude orientation...

I'm adding wisp ghosts around the shaft and near the cage, plus a ring of orbiting glowing octahedron motes near the top. I'm also setting bone-colored flat material for the dragon claw prongs, and double-checking the loft and sweep function signatures along with the ivory color bands for the horns.

Now I'm writing the blade geometry: defining a Bezier curve with control points for the blade's edge profile, functions to compute tangents, a knot-based scaling function for subtle width ripples along the length, and a width function tapering the blade with a slight sinusoidal bulge.

I'm sampling points along the spine and edge curves at the knots and merging them, building the outline by combining spine points with reversed edge points while marking sharp corners at the root and tip where width goes to zero.

For the edge glow sweep, I'm building a polyline along the edge path from root to tip and tapering its radius linearly, keeping an eye on cost since adaptive ring sampling across ~90 points could get expensive.

I'm also setting up the spine as a thick bone-like tube at the centerline, much wider than the blade itself for that dragon-bone aesthetic, with spikes along it computed from tangent and normal offsets that shrink in length and radius toward the tip.

Now I'm working out glyph placement — trying to fit them between the diagonal ribs that run from spine to edge, since the gaps between ribs are fairly narrow. I'm reconsidering the midpoint math between knot points to avoid overlap with the ribs, and thinking it might be simpler to shift the glyphs toward the scalloped edge valleys instead.

Checking where ribs cross the glyph plane confirms placing glyphs at f=0.78 near the valley midpoints keeps them clear of rib paths, since ribs cross that level earlier in t. Now I'm working out valley depth.

Maybe I should place glyphs on the wider root segment instead, before the first rib, stacking 2-3 there. Or I could simplify to just 4 ribs total with adjusted knot positions, letting the large root panel hold a bigger glyph.

I'm thinking a dragon-eye sigil (ellipse, vertical slit, rays in teal) works well as the main emblem near the root, with smaller valley glyphs scattered at shallower points. I need to double check that the root mounting plate doesn't overlap or clash with where this emblem sits.

Writing color stops for the blade gradient...

Still writing orb and rune geometry...

Extruding the dais hexagon outline along the x-axis cross y-axis direction, verifying the thickness orientation maps correctly to world-space y and the outline depth centers properly around the specified origin point.

Working out the three stacked tiers now: a base tier at radius 0.78, a middle tier at radius 0.7, and a top tier at radius 0.56, each stacked vertically with small gaps closing between 0 and 0.16 in height. I'm also planning a thin gold hexagonal trim swept along the tier boundary, sized slightly smaller than the tier's edge radius so it sits inset within the top surface.

Now I'm figuring out closed-polyline sweeps for the trims — making sure the four-sided path closes properly so the rounded caps meet seamlessly at the corners, then placing trim rings at the tier2 rim and tier0 top. For the hex side inlays, I'm calculating the apothem distance for tier1 and mapping each face's outward direction using 60-degree increments so I can position small flattened gem shapes centered on each side, converting the 2D outline coordinates into world-space x/z positions.

Defining a helper function to convert radius and angle into world coordinates, then using it to place corner posts and skull/paint spheres with mottled UV-based coloring. Now I'm scattering floating motes along the shaft at randomized angles, radii, and heights while avoiding the blade region, and placing a ring of ghostly soul shapes at varying heights and radial spread with outward-facing, radially flowing animation.

Adjusting ghost positions to dodge the prong geometry near the base, then adding glowing card elements for the ghosts and flame effects at the post tips, mouth, and crown area to give the piece more fiery accents. Now I'm starting to lay out the chain/charm geometry anchored to the hook position.

Writing chain spans and joints...

Writing vertebra function...

Still defining spine geometry...

I'm checking the sweep and cards helper signatures and how frame() handles the position and direction inputs, plus confirming bone attachments for the skull and horn geometry use consistent model-space coordinates before I commit to writing the full file.

Working through horn curve control points, aiming for an outward sweep that curls back and up, and tallying the overall height so the skull plus horns land around 2.34 units -- then double-checking the horn on the opposite side doesn't collide with the hook geometry near the top.

I'm sketching a second, smaller horn pair that sweeps down and back along the cheek, then designing the eye sigil as an SVG emblem with an almond outline, iris circle, slit pupil, and radiating lines, scaled to match the teal stroke styling.

Starting to write the final part geometry code...

Good enough, time to write the file now.
